subject: Clarify: Do you train models on customer data? / retention & deletion details
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@astrahealthcare.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: security@astrahealthcare.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Data use question — training on customer data?

Hi Vivek,

Quick question from our procurement/security review: does Redwood ever use customer prompt/response traffic to train or fine-tune models (either internally or with third parties)? Astra needs a short written assurance we can include in our vendor assessment.

A few follow ups it would be great to have answered in one note:
- Do you ever incorporate production requests into model training datasets?
- What is the default retention window for API request/response logs and KV caches?
- If we request deletion, what is the expected SLA and are backups included?
- Are there configuration options for customers to opt out of any telemetry retained for platform operations?

We have a deadline for the security packet on Friday. Appreciate anything concise we can add.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Senior Manager, Vendor Risk
Astra Healthcare
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@astrahealthcare.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Data use question — training on customer data?

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answer for your packet: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response traffic to train or update our public model weights by default. Below is a concise summary and I will loop in Neha (privacy) and Marcus (platform) for the detailed technical/operational points.

Bullet summary you can paste: 
- Non-training guarantee: Redwood does not train or fine-tune production models on customer API requests. Customer traffic is isolated from datasets used for model development.
- Retention: Default request/response logs are kept for 30 days for debugging/observability and then purged; longer retention is available only under contract.
- Deletion SLA: Customer-initiated deletion requests are processed within 72 hours; we also purge from active caches and mark backups for expiration per our backup retention policy.
- Opt-outs: Customers can enable a strict telemetry opt-out tier (no request-level logs retained) for Dedicated/Private plans and for hosted customers via an enterprise contract.

Neha — can you add a short technical note about KV/cache behavior and backup handling and attach the one-page assurance doc? Marcus — can you confirm the 72-hour deletion SLA covers both live caches and search/indexes so Emily can include that in the packet.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Privacy (inferred)
Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@astrahealthcare.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Data use question — training on customer data? (details & artifacts)

Hi Emily — putting the operational details below, plus two attachments: (1) a one-page Non-Training Assurance you can include in your vendor packet and (2) a simplified diagram of our retention/deletion flow.

Operational details (concise):
- Training separation: Production API traffic is ingested into a separate telemetry cluster used for observability and billing, which is logically and access-controlled away from research/modeling datasets. We do not copy production prompts/responses into datasets used to train our models or share raw customer data with third-party training vendors.
- Sampling & annotations: We may use anonymized/consented data from community sources for research experiments; this is never sourced from customer production traffic unless explicitly contracted and consented.
- KV cache: Ephemeral KV caches used for inference are stored on-node and are cleared when instances are deprovisioned. For long-running sessions in Dedicated deployments, KV entries are retained only for the session lifetime unless the customer opts into a longer cache policy.
- Logs & retention windows: Default hosted retention = 30 days (request/response, error traces, metrics). Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention via policy up to contract limits.
- Deletion process & backups: Deletion request flow: (a) customer requests deletion via Console/API -> (b) we stop accepting related telemetry and trigger immediate purge on active systems -> (c) mark records in backup catalogue for expedited expiration. Backups are not immediately shredded; they are excluded from restore and scheduled for deletion within the backup retention acceleration window (standard: 90 days, expedited per contract). Our standard SLA to complete deletion from active systems and mark backups is 72 hours; full physical deletion from all backup media follows the backup lifecycle unless a specific contractual shredding commitment is agreed.
- Auditability & evidence: We maintain an audit log of deletion requests and actions. SOC 2 reports and our internal deletion runbook can be shared under NDA.

Attachments: redwood-non-training-assurance.pdf (one-page) — includes plain-language assurance and a contact for escalation. retention-deletion-flow-diagram.png — simplified operational flow.

If Astra requires a shorter sentence for the vendor packet, use: "Redwood Inference does not use customer production requests to train model weights or datasets; request-level telemetry is retained per contract and can be fully removed on request per our deletion SLA."

Happy to hop on a quick call if you need more context.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
